correctness.rationale: The alternating Hall bracket and Jacobi give the coordinate map (det(f,g), f gamma'-g gamma, fe-gd). The Hall vectors span by degree and their leading associative word coefficients include units in every characteristic, including the mixed degree-four vector. If det(f,g) is prescribed nonzero, f has q^2-1 choices, g has q, the gamma coordinates are uniquely determined by U, and (d,e) has q lifts per V. If w=0 and U is nonzero, the line [U] is forced for the nonzero dependent pair (f,g); the two scalar entries have q^2-1 choices, and the remaining linear equations have q and q^2 lifts exactly when U divides V. Both cases include q^6 free central coordinates. The original formulas for central fibers are also correct: for nonzero C they are recovered from quotient commuting probabilities by linear scaling and subtraction of the nonsplit-line aggregate; at zero the recovered formula is q^12+(q+1)q^9(q^2-1). For image size the noncentral contributions are (q-1)q^5 and (q^2-1)q^2; the central nonzero count uses unordered pairs of linear factors with repetition, followed by q-1 choices of scalar. Width is exactly two since a nonsplit central quadratic is excluded and [L,L]=[x,L]+[y,L]. The corrected files preserve these checks and distinguish what is recovered from prior work. The supplied finite-field checker and output were inspected, not executed; the algebraic computation establishes every prime power.

value.rationale: The repaired result exhausts both noncentral target strata of the natural commutator map in the first rank-two class with a genuinely mixed linear/quadratic obstruction. It distinguishes a fixed nonzero degree-two layer with full uniform fibers from the mixed layer where a prescribed cubic direction forces quartic divisibility, and gives sizes over every finite field including characteristic two. This is a useful target-resolved invariant not captured by commuting probabilities, known width, or an arbitrary finite slice.
